questions.question: Globalization refers to
choices: the end of all international communication
growing connections among people, economies, and societies across national borders
the isolation of local economies
a political system used by every country

questions.question: A supply chain is
choices: a list of a company's employees
a treaty that sets national borders
the network of steps and organizations involved in producing and delivering a good
a system for measuring population density

questions.question: How can digital communication contribute to globalization?
choices: It prevents people from contacting other countries
It makes transportation unnecessary for every product
It eliminates differences in language
It allows information and services to move quickly across long distances

questions.question: A company designs a product in one country, sources parts in several others, and assembles it elsewhere. This is an example of
choices: a global supply chain
subsistence production
economic isolation
local barter only

questions.question: What is outsourcing?
choices: Moving all production back to the home country
Contracting work or services to an outside provider, sometimes in another country
Eliminating all paid work
Exchanging goods without prices

questions.question: Why might companies relocate production to another country?
choices: To avoid all shipping and communication
Because international laws require every firm to relocate
To access workers, suppliers, markets, or lower costs
To eliminate competition from local businesses

questions.question: Which group helps set and monitor rules for international trade among its members?
choices: International Court of Justice only
World Health Organization
North Atlantic Treaty Organization
World Trade Organization

questions.question: A product's price rises after a key port closes. What does this show about global supply chains?
choices: A disruption in one location can affect production and prices elsewhere
Supply chains are always local
Ports have no effect on trade
Prices cannot respond to transportation changes

questions.question: What is cultural diffusion?
choices: The measurement of national income
The spread of cultural ideas or practices between groups
The movement of tectonic plates
A type of agricultural irrigation

questions.question: Why can globalization create both opportunities and challenges for workers?
choices: It guarantees higher wages for every worker
It prevents industries from changing
It can expand markets and jobs while also increasing competition and restructuring employment
It eliminates differences in working conditions

questions.question: What is one possible environmental effect of increased global trade?
choices: Trade always reduces resource consumption
Trade has no connection to transportation
Global shipping eliminates pollution
More transportation and production can increase emissions and resource use

questions.question: A country exports a large share of its products to one trading partner. What risk may it face?
choices: A downturn or policy change in that partner's market may reduce export demand
Its exports become independent of foreign demand
The partner cannot affect trade
Its currency can never fluctuate

questions.question: What does the digital divide describe?
choices: The difference between two computer file formats
Unequal access to digital technologies and reliable internet
A gap between a country's borders and its coast
The spread of a language through migration

questions.question: Why is comparative advantage used to explain some patterns of international trade?
choices: Every country produces every good at identical cost
Trade requires countries to have the same resources
Countries can benefit by specializing in goods with lower opportunity costs and trading
Comparative advantage guarantees equal incomes

questions.question: A global clothing brand changes its advertising to fit local languages and customs. This is an example of
choices: ending cultural exchange
replacing all local businesses
eliminating a supply chain
adapting a global product or message to local contexts

questions.question: How can migration contribute to globalization?
choices: People carry skills, languages, ideas, and family connections across borders
Migration prevents cultural and economic ties
Migrants cannot affect labor markets
Migration occurs only during wars

questions.question: Why should consumers examine where and how a product is made?
choices: A product's origin determines its quality with certainty
Production conditions can affect labor rights, environmental impacts, and costs
Supply chains never involve multiple firms
Origin labels replace the need for evidence

questions.question: A region attracts call-center jobs serving customers in another time zone. Which factor likely supports this service trade?
choices: The region's distance from the internet
The absence of language skills
Communication technology and access to workers
A lack of international connections

questions.question: What is one potential benefit of international cooperation on climate change?
choices: Each country's emissions affect only its own territory
Cooperation eliminates every disagreement
Climate conditions are identical worldwide
Countries can coordinate goals and actions for a problem that crosses borders

questions.question: A news story claims globalization benefits everyone equally. Which evidence would best test that claim?
choices: Compare wages, job changes, prices, and gains across different groups and places
Count only the total value of exports
Measure the number of international flights
Use one company's profits as the only indicator
